I been farming these fields 40 years, so I do same as last year mostly. That way works. My land is 34.1 mu, all wheat then maize, one after the other like everyone here.

For wheat, I plant in October. I buy hybrid seed from the dealer in town — the one my neighbor Old Wang uses, his wheat last year was good. Before planting I spread compound fertilizer, the 15-15-15 kind, about 50 jin per mu (that's 25 kg), then add urea at the green-up time in spring, maybe 30 jin per mu. This is what I done for many years. I plough the field after maize comes off, turn the stubble under. Water from the well — I water at planting, then before winter, then at jointing, then when grain is filling. Four times usually. For weeds and aphid I spray two times, sometimes three if the aphid is bad. Last year I got about 450 kg per mu, I hope same this year.

For maize, I plant right after wheat harvest in June, no time to plough so I just use rotary, drill the seed in. Hybrid seed, Zhengdan or similar — the dealer tells me what is good. I put compound fertilizer with the seed and then topdress urea when maize is knee-high. Maize don't need so much water because summer rain comes, but I water one or two times if dry. Spray for corn borer and armyworm, two times. Maize gives me 550 kg per mu usually.

My family is 7 people, some work in town, so for busy time I hire the combine harvester, costs money but I cannot do 34 mu alone at my age. I buy a bit more fertilizer than maybe needed — better than losing grain. Losing harvest is disaster, extra bag of urea is only few hundred yuan.
